samples.prompt: Write a reflective narrative about revisiting a memory from your youth involving an unfinished or newly constructed building. Describe your philosophical impressions of the empty structure at the time and include a specific incident or action you took during your visit.
samples.generated:
I went back to the <PLACE> and looked at the great white tower, which was
then half-finished and half-collapsed, and found that I had a certain
feeling of having come across something real in an unreal world. The
sense is hard to describe; it is like a sense of having met some
person who is only partly dead. There was in this building a kind of
life that had ceased, but not quite; its bones were still there. It was
as if some one had been caught in the act of jumping off a high cliff.
The whole thing was full of the air of an unfinished thing. It seemed to
me that if I threw myself off the top of that tower I should fall into
nothingness. If I threw myself into the sea I should fall into a sea of
nothingness. A man might be killed in either case. But he could not
possibly be born. And in the middle of all these reflections my mind
turned upon the fact that I was standing on the brink of the tower with
a knife in my hand. It was not for any particular pleasure that I
suddenly drew the blade of this dagger from my pocket, nor did I
particularly care whether I killed anyone or not, but I felt that if
anything must die it ought to be me. I have never forgotten that
moment.
